title: UK Authorizes SCALP/Storm Shadow Assembly in Ukraine as China Unveils Hypersonic Air-to-Air Missile
subhead: Britain released classified Storm Shadow blueprints to enable Ukrainian domestic missile production on Independence Day, while Bloomberg reported China has developed hypersonic glide vehicles that can launch air-to-air weapons — two moves that reshape the long-range strike picture in Europe and the Pacific.

sections.heading: UK Opens SCALP Assembly in Ukraine With First Classified Blueprint Release
sections.body: On Ukraine's 35th Independence Day, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced that Britain has authorized defense firm MBDA to release classified information on UK components used in the long-range Storm Shadow/SCALP cruise missile, enabling Ukraine to establish domestic assembly lines, according to AeroTime. The move follows talks in June between Ukraine and France on a SCALP production license. Russia's presidential spokesman Dmitry Peskov accused the UK of 'pouring fuel on the fire,' and Moscow said its forces are gathering data to identify and destroy the production sites. The announcement came as Burnham made his first visit to Kyiv, co-chairing a Coalition of the Willing summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the first time a Western ally has released classified missile-production blueprints to Ukraine, setting a precedent for technology transfer that goes beyond supplying finished weapons — and drawing a direct Russian threat to strike the new assembly sites.

sections.heading: China Develops Hypersonic Air-to-Air Missile Capability
sections.body: Bloomberg reported that the Chinese military has developed hypersonic glide vehicles (HGVs) that can launch air-to-air weapons, an advancement meant to threaten high-value targets such as command-and-control aircraft thousands of kilometres away. A person with direct knowledge said China also added air-to-air capabilities to some hypersonic cruise missiles and built anti-ship capabilities into several missile types. An HGV deployed from a DF-17 could travel about 2,414 km — just short of the distance to Guam — while the DF-27, with a maximum range of about 8,000 km, puts Hawaii in range. No other country is known to operate weapons combining an HGV with air-to-air missiles, per the report. The Pentagon estimates China had at least 3,150 ballistic missiles and 300 ground-launched cruise missiles as of 2024.
sections.whyItMatters: If confirmed, this would give the PLA a unique way to hold US tankers, AWACS and flying command posts at risk from extreme range — precisely the support aircraft the US Navy's new AIM-424 Malice and AIM-260 are being built to counter, underscoring the accelerating long-range air-to-air race.

sections.heading: US Munitions Stockpiles Drawn Down Sharply in Iran War
sections.body: Reuters reported that the US Army has used up much of its stockpile of highly accurate long-range missiles during its five-month war with Iran, with sources saying the US has used 'virtually all' of its ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM). A CSIS report estimates that between February and July the Army expended about 65 per cent of its Patriot interceptors, that THAAD interceptor stockpiles are at least 38 per cent lower than at the start of the war, and that the US burned through a little less than half of its global Tomahawk supply. The White House pushed back, with President Trump saying the US has 'far more munitions than anyone in the world.' Raytheon, a unit of RTX, has reached a tentative multi-year agreement with the Pentagon to boost Tomahawk production.
sections.whyItMatters: The drawdown of ATACMS/PrSM — weapons analysts say would be critical in any conflict with China — and of Patriot/THAAD interceptors is the clearest signal yet of how the Iran war is straining US readiness for a potential Pacific contingency, even as production ramps up.

sections.heading: US Cancels South Korea Marine Drill on Iran War Force Constraints
sections.body: Reuters reported that the United States cancelled a joint amphibious landing drill scheduled for next month with South Korea, with Seoul's Marine Corps citing constraints on the availability of US forces due to the war in Iran. The cancellation follows President Trump's order last week to scale down the separate annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises. The Philadelphia Inquirer noted the decision has intensified doubts over Washington's capacity to manage concurrent global conflicts as US weapons and forces are stretched.
sections.whyItMatters: Cancelling a scheduled allied exercise in the Indo-Pacific to free forces for the Middle East is a concrete, visible cost of the Iran war on US posture toward North Korea and China — a burden-sharing signal Seoul and regional allies will read carefully.

sections.heading: Australia Lays Keel of First Hunter-Class Frigate
sections.body: BAE Systems Australia laid the keel of NUSHIP Hunter, the first of Australia's Type 26-derived Hunter-class anti-submarine warfare frigates, at Osborne Naval Shipyard on 24 August, joined by Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy and Chief of Navy Vice Admiral Matthew Buckley. The Hunter class is central to Australia's effort to build a continuous sovereign naval shipbuilding capability. However, reports of a weight surge threaten the vessel's acoustic quieting and submarine-hunting stealth, and Defence Minister Richard Marles has blamed previous Coalition governments for the weight problems, per The Australian. The ship is expected for delivery in the early 2030s.
sections.whyItMatters: The keel-laying marks a milestone in Australia's A$45 billion sovereign shipbuilding program, but the reported weight growth — which could undermine the very anti-submarine mission the class is designed for — remains a live risk as the program moves from fabrication to assembly.

sections.heading: India Test-Fires Fully Indigenous AK-203 'Sher' Rifle
sections.body: On 23 August, India successfully test-fired the first 100 per cent indigenised AK-203 'Sher' rifle at the Korwa Ordnance Factory in Amethi, according to Firstpost. Major General SK Sharma, CEO of Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited (IRRPL), said every component and input material was sourced from Indian industry — 'true, end-to-end 100% genuine indigenisation.' The rifle, a modern Kalashnikov variant firing the 7.62x39 mm cartridge, will undergo Indian Army trials in September, with plans to deliver over six lakh rifles by 2030-2032 as a replacement for the Insas. Domestic content had reached only 50 per cent by mid-2025.
sections.whyItMatters: The milestone shows India cracking the Kalashnikov supply chain entirely domestically — a step in its Atmanirbhar Bharat defense self-reliance drive that reduces dependence on Russian components even as the weapon's design remains Russian-origin.

sections.heading: Sweden's Gripen Gains Deep-Strike With First TAURUS Launch
sections.body: On 21 August, the Swedish Air Force conducted the first launch of a TAURUS KEPD 350 cruise missile from a JAS-39 Gripen C at the Vidsel Test Range, according to Opex360. The Taurus, developed with Saab and MBDA Deutschland, carries a 495 kg Mephisto warhead and can strike targets up to 500 km away at Mach 0.95. Sweden, which had no offensive air-to-air counter-strike capability, ordered the missiles in 2024 to gain deep-strike deterrence against Russia, targeting an IOC in 2028 — though Air Force commander Gen. Jonas Wikman said integration could be completed well before that. Sweden will field 60 Gripen C/D at MS20 Block 4 standard by 2028.
sections.whyItMatters: The first Taurus launch gives Sweden a long-range standoff strike option it previously lacked, a significant capability shift for a NATO's newest member facing Russia across the Baltic — and a boost for the Taurus program, already in service with Germany, Spain and South Korea.

bottomLine: The dominant theme of the day is the long-range strike race. Britain's decision to hand Ukraine classified Storm Shadow blueprints for domestic assembly marks a genuine escalation in Western technology transfer — moving from supplying weapons to enabling their production — while Bloomberg's report on China's hypersonic air-to-air missile capability shows Beijing pushing the same envelope in the Pacific. Beneath both sits the strain of the Iran war: the US has burned through most of its ATACMS/PrSM and a large share of its Patriot and Tomahawk stocks, and has cancelled a scheduled South Korea drill to free forces. Australia's Hunter-class keel-laying, India's fully indigenous AK-203, and Sweden's first Taurus launch round out a day defined by production, sovereignty and reach.
sources: AeroTime, Reuters, Bloomberg, Straits Times, Kyiv Independent, DefenseScoop, Firstpost, Opex360, UK Defence Journal, The Australian, Philadelphia Inquirer, CSIS
